en.title: Subordinating conjunctions
en.summary: A subordinating conjunction introduces a dependent clause.

paragraphs: A subordinating conjunction introduces a clause that depends on the main clause and cannot stand alone. The dependent clause gives time, cause, condition, contrast, purpose or result.

items: I stayed home **because** it was raining.
He works hard **so that** he can succeed.

blocks.html:
MeaningConjunctionsExample
timewhen, while, before, after, until, as soon asI'll call when I arrive.
causebecause, since, asI stayed because I was ill.
conditionif, unless, provided thatUnless you hurry, you'll be late.
contrastalthough, though, even though, whereasAlthough it rained, we went out.
purposeso that, in order thatI left early so that I wouldn't be late.
resultso... that, such... thatIt was so cold that we stayed in.
placewhere, whereverStay where you are.

paragraphs: The dependent clause can come first or second. If it comes first, put a comma after it; if it comes second, usually no comma: Because it was late, we left. We left because it was late.

blocks.html:
Dependent clause firstMain clause first
When she called, I was out.I was out when she called.
If you want, I'll help.I'll help if you want.

sections.title: A dependent clause alone is not a sentence

paragraphs: A dependent clause must be attached to a main clause. Because it was raining is not a sentence by itself; it needs a main clause: We stayed home because it was raining.

items: Wrong: **Because it rained.** (as a sentence) Right: **We stayed home because it rained.**
Wrong: **Although it was cold, but we went out.** Right: **Although it was cold, we went out.**
Wrong: **When I will arrive, I'll call.** Right: **When I arrive, I'll call.**
